name: Automations
description: Automate repetitive work without writing code: appointment reminders, low-stock alerts and messages to customers that go out on their own.

ui.aiMaxIters: How many turns it may take
ui.aiMaxItersHint: {max} at most. Every turn is a real call, and every call costs money.
ui.aiPolicyAuto: Let it go ahead on its own
ui.aiPolicyAutoWarning: It will change your data with nobody watching, at any hour. Only choose this once you have seen it propose the right thing several times.
ui.aiPolicyManualHint: Anything it wants to change waits for you under “Waiting for you”. Nothing happens until you say so.
ui.aiPromptHint: Write it as you would to a person, and insert fields from what happened. Never put a key or a password here: it would be sent to the assistant.
ui.aiToolsHint: Offering something here does not allow it. Each one still has to be allowed on the Permissions tab.
ui.aiToolsTitle: What it may look at and do
ui.approvalAskedAdmins: Asked of whoever manages the hub.
ui.approvalAskedRole: Asked of: {role}. Whoever manages the hub can answer too.
ui.approvalAssigneeHint: A role, never a person: people leave, roles stay. Whoever manages the hub can always answer, so a question never gets stuck.
ui.approvalContinueHint: Carrying on means the next steps run whatever the answer was. Add a condition on {path} (approved, rejected or expired) right after this step to do different things for each answer.
ui.approvalErrAlreadyDecided: Somebody already answered this one. Nothing was done twice.
ui.approvalErrExpired: Too late: this one expired before you answered. Nothing was done.
ui.approvalErrNotYours: This question was asked of another role, and you cannot answer it. Nothing was done.
ui.approvalExpires: If you do nothing, this expires on {when} and never runs.
ui.approvalExpiresIn: How long to wait for an answer
ui.approvalExpiresInHint: At most 30 days. When the time runs out the automation does what you choose below — it never stays waiting forever.
ui.approvalExpires_cancel: If nobody answers by {when}, the automation stops here.
ui.approvalExpires_continue: If nobody answers by {when}, the automation carries on anyway.
ui.approvalExpires_reject: If nobody answers by {when}, it counts as a no.
ui.approvalOnExpire_continue: Carry on with the next steps
ui.approvalOnReject_continue: Carry on with the next steps
ui.approvalOutputsHint: The next steps can use {paths} — only if the automation carries on past this step.
ui.approvalTitleHint: This is what the person will read. It is filled in the moment the question is asked — editing the automation afterwards does not change a question already waiting.
ui.approvalsIntro: The assistant wants to change something. Nothing has happened yet.
ui.checkupEchoBody: It was set up before we corrected it, so it also reacts to the replies you send from your own phone and to conversations from months ago. Update it and it will only react to what a customer writes now. Nothing else about it changes.
ui.checkupEchoTitle: This automation also runs on your own messages
ui.checkupReplyTitle: A customer’s answer may count for two automations
ui.checkupReplyBody: It checks the answer to a question that another automation also asks, so a «Yes» to one counts for both. Open it and choose the question again.
ui.checkupFixed: “{name}” now only reacts to what a customer writes.
ui.checkupNotFixed: We could not update this automation: the hub saved it without the change. Try again in a moment, and tell support if it keeps happening.
ui.commandHint: The name of a command in this hub, for example sales.sale.create. You will be asked to allow it before it can run.
ui.copyMade: Copied, and the copy is paused. It carries none of the original's permissions — allow what it needs before turning it on.
ui.copySecrets: It reaches out using: {names}. Check those are the right ones for the copy.
ui.cronKept: This schedule is more detailed than this screen can draw, so it is shown as it is and left exactly as it is. Nothing here can change it by accident.
ui.cronMonthdayHint: A month shorter than the day you pick simply skips it, so day 31 does not run in February.
ui.cronSimplify: Replace it with a simple schedule
ui.deadClosedIntro: The hub keeps who closed each one, when and why for ninety days.
ui.deadClosedNoReason: {event} — closed, with no reason written down.
ui.deadDenied: Automations has not been allowed to see what got stuck. Open Settings → Permissions and allow it.
ui.deadDiscardConfirm: Close this for good? It stops counting and nothing will ever send it again.
ui.deadDiscardReasonHint: We already record who closed it and when. Why is the part only you know — it is optional, but it is what makes this readable in six months.
ui.deadDiscardReasonNotKept: {event} is closed, but this hub is older than the reason field, so it kept who and when and not why. Updating it is what turns that on.
ui.deadDiscardReasonPlaceholder: Optional — e.g. the invoice was registered by hand
ui.deadDoRetry: If you have fixed what caused it, send it again.
ui.deadDoRevoked: Allow it again in Permissions and run the automation. Sending this one again would fail for the same reason.
ui.deadIntro: These never happened. Decide what to do with each one.
ui.deadRetriedAll: {count} sent again. If the cause is still there they will come back.
ui.deadRevoked: You took away the permission this needed while it was still waiting, so it can never go out as it stands.
ui.deadUnexplained: It stopped, and what is folded below is everything the hub was told about why.
ui.deadUnsupported: This hub is older than this screen, so it cannot tell you whether anything got stuck. Updating it is what turns this on.
ui.deleteConfirm: Delete «{name}»? There is no undoing this.
ui.deleteMessage: It stops running immediately. Its history stays as the record that it existed.
ui.emptyMessage: An automation watches for something happening in your business and then does something about it — on its own, every time.
ui.enableNoGrants: On, but it does not hold the permissions it asks for yet ({commands}): it will do nothing until you grant them on the Permissions tab.
ui.enableUntested: You have not tried it yet: the Try it tab shows what it would do before it runs on its own.
ui.errGeneric: Something went wrong. Nothing was saved.
ui.errLimitNotApplied: The recipe was installed and left switched off, with no permission granted: this hub could not store the limit it needs. Turning it on with the wide permission would let it do more than the recipe promises. Do not grant it by hand in Permissions: that puts the wide permission back. Leave it as it is — the recipe will start working on its own once this hub is updated.
ui.errRestoreFailed: The automation could not be restored. Nothing was changed; try again in a moment.
ui.errRestoreGone: This automation no longer exists here, so there is nothing to restore. Activate it again from its app.

ui.evHostPrint: this device is asked to print

ui.evModifierDetached: a modifier is taken off a product

ui.evOrderFired: an order is fired to the kitchen

ui.evRecordRejected: the tax office rejects an invoice

ui.evStockChanged: the stock of a product changes

ui.evaUncategorized: is taken out of its category
ui.eventCatalogDenied: Automations may not read this hub’s events yet. Grant it in Settings → Permissions, then reopen this flow.
ui.eventCatalogEmpty: This hub does not have any event yet. Install a module that produces some — meanwhile, type the exact name below.
ui.eventCatalogFailed: This hub could not list its events ({code}). Type the exact name below.
ui.eventCatalogLoading: Asking this hub which events it can fire…
ui.eventCatalogUnsupported: This hub is too old to list its own events. Update it to pick from a list — meanwhile, type the exact name below.
ui.eventNoSamples: No examples yet: nothing like this has happened here in the last 90 days
ui.eventNotInHub: This hub does not have it — it comes with the {module} module
ui.eventOtherHint: Type the exact name of an event this hub emits.
ui.fieldReplyToStep: The step that asked the question
ui.fieldReplyToFlow: The automation that asked the question
ui.replyStepAmbiguous: Two automations ask this same question. Choose it again so the answer only counts for the one you mean.
ui.replyStepMissing: A question that no longer exists — choose another
ui.replyStepNone: None of your automations sends a WhatsApp yet. Add a WhatsApp step that asks the question, then come back here.
ui.replyStepLoadFailed: Your automations could not be loaded, so the questions cannot be listed.
ui.grantCommandNotFound: This hub has no command called {command}. Check the name in the step.
ui.grantLimitBadRoot: «{field}» names something this automation does not have. A limit can only use what the automation itself works out — write input.… or steps.… — or a fixed value.
ui.grantLimitBadTemplate: «{field}» cannot be written with {{…}}. Write the value on its own — steps.find_customer.id — so the automation compares it as it is.
ui.grantLimitsIntro: Fix a value and this automation may only act with that value. Anything else it tries is refused — and so is leaving the field out, so it cannot get round the limit by staying quiet.
ui.grantLimitsNone: No limits: it may do this with whatever it decides.
ui.grantLimitsRef: A limit can be a fixed value, or what this automation works out each time it runs: write steps.find_customer.id and it will only ever act on the customer of that conversation.
ui.grantsIntro: An automation runs with its own permissions, never with yours. Nothing below happens until you allow it.
ui.grantsNone: This automation asks for nothing yet.
ui.guardExplain: If this is not true the automation stops here. It does not do anything else — there is no second path.
ui.httpGrantHint: This step will ask you to allow calls to {pattern}
ui.httpGrantUnknown: Fill in the address and this step will tell you what it needs you to allow.
ui.httpHeadersHint: Where a key or a token goes. Save it as a secret below, then insert it here — its value is never shown again.
ui.httpTimeoutHint: Seconds, {max} at most. The automation is held up for the whole wait — including when it ends in an error.
ui.listSearch: Search by name, by what starts it or by what it does
ui.noAccessMessage: Automations can run commands while nobody is watching, so this module only reaches them if you allow it. Go to Settings → Permissions and turn on “Manage automations” for Automations.
ui.noSteps: No steps yet. Add the first thing this automation should do.
ui.notAdminMessage: An automation acts in the name of the business without anybody watching, so deciding what it may do is not something a shift session can approve.
ui.notAdminTitle: Only an owner or an administrator can edit automations
ui.notifyModeHint: A message with options comes back as a tap you can react to, instead of free text somebody has to read.
ui.notifyTemplateHint: On WhatsApp, the template Meta approved for you. On email it becomes the subject, unless you write one yourself.
ui.notifyTemplatePickHint: The templates Meta approved for your business. Without one, the message only reaches a customer who wrote to you in the last 24 hours.
ui.notifyTemplateNone: No template — plain text (last 24 hours only)
ui.notifyTemplatesEmpty: You have no template approved by Meta yet. Bring them in from WhatsApp → Templates.
ui.notifyTemplatesError: Your WhatsApp templates could not be read. You can still write the name of the template by hand.
ui.notifyTemplateUnknown: “{name}” is not among your approved templates: WhatsApp will not send it. Choose one from the list.
ui.notifyHeaderDeduced: This template carries a file at the top ({kind}): add the link to it.
ui.notifyHeaderUnsupported: This template carries a file at the top ({kind}) and this hub cannot send it yet. Update the hub, or choose a template without one.
ui.notifyHeaderHint: If Meta approved this template with an image, video or document at the top, choose it here: without it WhatsApp does not send the message.
ui.notifyTitleValue: What goes in the gap of the template's title
ui.notifyTitleUnsupported: This template has a gap in its title and this hub cannot fill it yet. Update the hub, or choose a template without one.
ui.notifyLinkValue: End of the link of the «{button}» button
ui.notifyLinkUnsupported: This template has a link button that changes with each message and this hub cannot fill it yet. Update the hub, or choose a template without one.
ui.notifyToHint: The address is read from your own data and can never be typed here. That is what stops a message going to whatever arrived with the event.
ui.notifyWhatsappCost: Meta charges for every WhatsApp. An email costs nothing.
ui.opInHint: Separate the values with a comma.
ui.pickFieldNoSamples: This hub has not seen this happen recently, so there are no examples to show. The fields are still the right ones.
ui.pickFieldRedacted: example hidden: it could be about a person
ui.pickFieldSearch: Search by name or by value
ui.pickFieldSkipArray: not offered: it is a list, and an automation cannot reach inside one
ui.pickFieldSkipObject: not offered on its own: pick one of the fields inside it
ui.queryHint: The name of a read in this hub, for example inventory.stock.low. It has to exist here, and you will be asked to allow it before it runs. Nothing is changed by looking something up.
ui.queryLimitHint: Between 1 and {max}. The hub refuses more instead of quietly cutting the read short.
ui.queryOutputsHint: The next steps can use {paths}. If nothing is found the automation carries on with found = false — add a condition on it to stop there.
ui.queryResult_first: The first row it finds, field by field
ui.ranGuardStopped: The condition was not met, so it stopped here. That is the automation working.
ui.ranNothingToOffer: There was nothing to offer (the list was empty), so the message was not sent
ui.readOnlyStep: This step keeps working. Editing it needs a newer version of this module.
ui.runCopied: Copied. Paste it if you ask us about this run.
ui.runStarted: It is running. Its result appears here in a moment.
ui.runWaitingApproval: Waiting for you to approve it
ui.secretSaved: {name} saved. Its value cannot be shown again.
ui.secretsIntro: Keys and passwords for other systems live here, encrypted. Once saved, a value can never be read back — not by you, not by this screen. Only a step that calls another system can use one.
ui.stepAiAuto: Asks the assistant: {prompt} — it changes things on its own
ui.stepAiEmpty: Write what you want the assistant to do
ui.stepAiManual: Asks the assistant: {prompt} — you approve any change
ui.stepApprovalEmpty: Write the question somebody has to answer
ui.stepHttpEmpty: Pick the address this step calls
ui.stepHttpTemplatedHost: Calls whatever address the data says ({method})
ui.stepNotifyEmail: Sends an email to the {field} on file
ui.stepNotifyEmpty: Pick who this message goes to
ui.stepNotifyWhatsapp: Sends a WhatsApp to the {field} on file
ui.stepUnsupported: A “{kind}” step, which this editor cannot edit yet
ui.tapBodyBlank: The message is empty — that is the line above the options.
ui.tapDuplicateId: Two options are named «{id}». A later check cannot tell them apart.
ui.tapKindHint_button: Up to {max} buttons, side by side under the message.
ui.tapKindHint_list: A button that opens a list of up to {max} choices.
ui.tapOpenLabel: The button that opens the list
ui.tapOpenLabelBlank: The button that opens the list has no text on it.
ui.tapOptionBlank: An option has no name or nothing written on it.
ui.tapOptionsHint: Whatever they tap comes back as «the option they tapped», so a later check can tell one from another.
ui.tapTooMany: WhatsApp shows at most {max}. The rest will not go out.
ui.testBlanksFound: {count} things would come out empty. That is almost always the mistake.
ui.testBlanksFoundOne: 1 thing would come out empty. That is almost always the mistake.
ui.testHidden: there is a value, and it is not shown here
ui.testNoRealData: This has not happened in your hub recently, so there is no real example to try it with. The steps below are still the right ones, but there is nothing to fill them in with.
ui.testNotReached: It would not get this far.
ui.testSkipped: Skipped this time: its "only if" does not hold with this data. The rest carries on.
ui.testMaySkip: May be skipped: its "only if" depends on something only known when the flow really runs.
ui.testNothingHappened: Nothing here is real. No message is sent, nothing is charged and nothing is written down — this is only what your automation WOULD do.
ui.testPausesHere: Waits here for somebody to answer. Testing does not answer for them: all three outcomes are still possible.
ui.testStoppedIsWorking: It would stop here, and that is the automation working: there is no second path.
ui.testTriggerBlocked: It would not even start: what happened does not match what you asked for.
ui.testUncertain: This cannot be checked here: it looks at something the hub hides because it could be about a person. It may go either way.
ui.testUnknown: comes from an earlier step, so it is only known once it has run
ui.testUsingReal: Using what really happened the last time {event}, from the last {count} of them in your own hub.
ui.testWouldBeRefused: It would be refused: you have not allowed {what} yet.
ui.tplCreatedPaused: It is created paused. Nothing happens until you turn it on.
ui.tplFromAppPlain: This automation comes with {app}, the app you have installed. It was written by the people who made the app, and it is created switched off like any other.
ui.tplGrantLimited: Only with {fields} — it cannot ask for anything else.
ui.tplGrantsIntro: An automation runs with its own permissions, never with yours. Until you allow these, it does nothing.
ui.tplGrantsTitle: What it will ask you to allow
ui.tplHaveItAlready: You already have this one. Open it to see how it is set up — using it again leaves you with two automations doing the same thing at the same time.
ui.tplHiddenModule: Some automations are hidden: they need the {modules} module, and this hub does not have it. Install it from the marketplace and reload this screen.
ui.tplHiddenModules: Some automations are hidden: they need the {modules} modules, and this hub does not have them. Install them from the marketplace and reload this screen.
ui.tplLede: Pick one of these and it becomes yours, switched off, ready for you to look at before it does anything.
ui.tplModulesOldCore: This hub does not yet offer the automations that come with your apps. It will after its next update.
ui.tplModulesUnavailable: The automations that come with your apps could not be loaded. The ones below are still here; reload the screen to try again.
ui.tplNoBlanks: Nothing to fill in. It is ready as it is.
ui.tplOutdatedNotice: There is a new version of this automation.
ui.tplRestoreConfirm: Your changes to this automation will be replaced by the new version. It stays on or off exactly as it is now.
ui.tplRestored: Done: this automation is now the factory version.
ui.tplSameTrigger: Careful: «{flows}» already runs on the same thing happening. If you add this one too, BOTH will run every time — two appointments, two messages to the same customer. Turn the other one off first unless you really want both.
ui.tplSameTriggerMany: Careful: «{flows}» already run on the same thing happening. If you add this one too, they will ALL run every time — several appointments, several messages to the same customer. Turn the others off first unless you really want them all.
ui.tplStepsTitle: What it does, step by step
ui.tplUnfinishedHint: You started this one and never allowed it anything, so it does nothing yet. Open it to finish it.
ui.triggerKindAt: Once, at a date and time
ui.troubleApproval: Nobody answered in time, so it let go.
ui.troubleDoApproval: Run it again if it still needs doing, and give whoever approves it more room next time.
ui.troubleDoGone: Open it and check the steps. If it was edited while a run was in flight, this run cannot be finished.
ui.troubleDoPermission: Open Permissions and allow what it needs. Until you do, this will happen every time.
ui.troubleDoReach: Open the step that calls the other service and check the address, and the permission that goes with it.
ui.troubleDoRecipient: Open the message step and check who it goes to — the list it reads may be empty now.
ui.troubleDoSecret: Open the step that reaches outside and check the secret it uses is still there.
ui.troubleDoSetup: Open it and save it again — the editor will show what does not fit.
ui.troubleGone: Something it needed is no longer there.
ui.troublePermission: It tried to do something you have not allowed it to do, so it stopped.
ui.troubleReach: The address it tried to reach is not one it is allowed to reach.
ui.troubleRecipient: It could not work out who to send the message to.
ui.troubleSecret: It needs a password or a key it could not read.
ui.troubleSetup: There is something this hub cannot read in how the automation is written.
ui.unsupportedMessage: The automation kernel arrived in a newer version of the hub. Update the hub and this editor will find it.
ui.unsupportedTitle: This hub cannot do automations yet

grant.tasksCreate: Create a task in your list. It stays inside the hub and never writes to a customer.
grant.customersNote: Add a note to a customer's history. It does not change their details and it does not contact them.
grant.notifyWhatsapp: Answer on WhatsApp. Every message sent is billed by Meta.
grant.recipientWhatsapp: Write back on that same conversation, and to nobody else.
grant.customersList: Look the customer up by their phone number.
grant.customersCreate: Create the card when it is somebody new. It waits for you to approve it.
grant.servicesList: Read your service catalogue, to tell which one they are asking for and how long it takes.
grant.staffList: Read who works at the salon, so it proposes somebody who is really there.
grant.staffSchedules: Read a professional’s hours, so the slot is one they actually work.
grant.dayOpening: Ask when the salon opens that day, instead of working it out on its own.
grant.availabilitySlots: Ask which slots are really free on that date.
grant.availabilityCheck: Check the slot is still free before proposing it.
grant.appointmentsCreate: Book the appointment. It waits in the tray until you approve it.
grant.appointmentsListForCustomer: Read the appointments a customer already has, so it cancels or moves the right one and never guesses.
grant.appointmentsCancel: Cancel an appointment when the customer asks, and only ever as that customer: the appointment has to be hers. It waits in the tray until you approve it, and your own cancellation rules still apply.
grant.appointmentsReschedule: Move an appointment to another time when the customer asks, and only ever as that customer: the appointment has to be hers. It waits in the tray until you approve it, and your own notice rules still apply.
grant.reservationsSettings: To tell them what this restaurant takes — the party sizes, the notice it wants and whether it needs a phone or an email. It only reads them.
grant.reservationsTimeslots: To know which service windows you open on that day of the week, so it never offers a time you do not serve.
grant.reservationsSlotsCount: To see how many tables are really left in each window of that day, counted the way the booking gate counts them.
grant.reservationsBlockedDates: To know whether you are closed that day, or part of it, before it offers anything.
grant.reservationsCreate: To put the table in the book. Only with the day, the time and the number of people the guest gave.
grant.reservationsWaitlistCreate: To put them on the waiting list when the day is full and they ask to be called if a table frees up.
grant.appointmentsCancelAsCustomer: Cancel an appointment when the customer asks, and only ever as that customer: the appointment has to be hers, and your own cancellation rules still apply.
grant.appointmentsRescheduleAsCustomer: Move an appointment to another time when the customer asks, and only ever as that customer: the appointment has to be hers, and your own notice rules still apply.

welcome.name: Welcome every new customer
welcome.summary: Somebody new goes into your customer list and you get a reminder to say hello.
welcome.plain: When a new customer is added → wait one day → leave you the task of welcoming them.
welcome.blankWaitHint: One day to start with. A welcome that arrives while they are still walking out of the door is the one nobody makes.

bigSale.name: Write the big visits into the customer's card
bigSale.summary: Every time somebody spends more than the amount you choose, a note lands in their history.
bigSale.plain: When a sale is charged → only if it has a customer and comes to more than the amount you set → write a note in that customer's card.
bigSale.blankAmount: The amount that makes a sale a big one
bigSale.blankAmountHint: In cents: 10000 is 100,00 €. The hub keeps money in cents, so writing 100 here would mean one euro.
bigSale.noteContent: Big visit. Worth a personal welcome next time.

newStaff.name: Somebody joins the team
newStaff.summary: A new person is added to your staff and the setting-up jobs are waiting for you the same minute.
newStaff.plain: When somebody new is added to the team → leave you the task of setting them up: keys, access, uniform, the first shift.
newStaff.blankList: What has to be done for a new starter
newStaff.blankListHint: Whatever you always forget. Write it as one list in the task text — keys, till code, rota, who shows them around.
newStaff.taskTitle: Set up the new team member
newStaff.taskDescription: Keys and alarm code · access to the till · rota for the first week · who walks them round on day one.

whatsapp.name: Nobody's WhatsApp goes unanswered
whatsapp.summary: A message comes in and answering it lands on somebody's list straight away, before the day swallows it.
whatsapp.plain: When a message arrives on WhatsApp → leave the urgent task of reading it and answering.
whatsapp.blankWhoHint: One person, not «somebody». A task everybody can see is a task everybody assumes the other one took.
whatsapp.taskDescription: Read it in the inbox and answer. If it turns into a booking or an order, put it through as usual.

fiscalRejected.name: Warn me if an invoice does not reach the tax agency
fiscalRejected.summary: A billing record that is refused stops being something you only find out by opening a screen.
fiscalRejected.plain: When an invoice fails to register → leave an urgent task to check it.
fiscalRejected.blankWhoHint: Whoever fixes invoices. Leave it unassigned and it lands in the shared list, which is fine in a small shop.
fiscalRejected.taskTitle: An invoice has not been registered with the tax agency
fiscalRejected.taskDescription: Open VeriFactu, find the record marked as failed and read the reason. It can be the agency refusing it, or the connection never reaching it. Until it is registered, that invoice is not filed.

cashClose.name: When the till closes, somebody checks the day
cashClose.summary: The session is closed and the check lands on a list while the shop is still standing there.
cashClose.plain: When a till session is closed → leave the task of checking the count and the day's paperwork.
cashClose.blankWhoHint: Whoever cashes up. If that is you, leave it as it is.
cashClose.taskDescription: Count against the session · anything that did not add up · the day's invoices went out.

weekReview.name: Friday evening, look at the week
weekReview.summary: A weekly reminder to sit down with the numbers, on the evening you choose.
weekReview.plain: Every Friday at 18:00 → leave you the task of going through the week: what sold, what did not, what to order.
weekReview.blankWhenHint: Friday at 18:00 to start with. Put it when you are closing, not in the middle of service.
weekReview.taskDescription: What sold and what did not · what to reorder · anything still unpaid · next week's diary.

morning.name: Every morning, go through tomorrow's diary
morning.summary: A task waiting for you first thing, so nobody's appointment goes unconfirmed.
morning.plain: Every day at 9:00 → leave you the task of going through tomorrow's appointments and confirming them.
morning.blankTimeHint: 09:00 to start with. Put it when you open, not when you are already busy.
morning.taskTitle: Go through tomorrow's appointments and confirm them

noShow.name: Whoever did not turn up does not get lost
noShow.summary: The moment an appointment is marked as a no-show, calling them back becomes a task.
noShow.plain: When an appointment is marked as a no-show → leave you the task of calling them and offering another time.
noShow.taskTitle: Call whoever did not turn up and offer them another time

bigParty.name: Big tables get prepared
bigParty.summary: A large booking comes in and the room has its task before the day arrives.
bigParty.plain: When a reservation is taken → only if it is for more people than you set → leave the room the task of getting the table ready.
bigParty.blankSize: How many people make a table a big one
bigParty.blankSizeHint: Six to start with. Count the people, not the tables.

waAppointment.name: WhatsApp → appointment proposal
waAppointment.summary: Somebody asks for an appointment on WhatsApp: it answers at once, reads the diary and proposes a real slot for you to confirm.
waAppointment.plain: When somebody writes to your WhatsApp, this answers them straight away so nobody is left waiting, makes sure they have a customer card, works out which service they are asking for and how long it takes, and finds a slot the diary really has free with a professional who works at that hour. Then it proposes the appointment. Nothing is booked and no card is created until somebody at the salon approves it.

guide.title: How automations work
guide.whatBody: It is a rule you leave written down: when something happens in your business, the hub does something about it — on its own, every time, without anybody having to remember.
guide.whatExample: In a salon: the moment somebody is marked as not having turned up, a job appears on your list telling you to ring them and offer another time. Nobody has to notice. It is already there.
guide.whatCan: It is not only for your own team either: an automation can send your customer a message, ask the assistant to write something, or call another service you use. Those steps are set up on the step itself, inside the automation, like every other one.
guide.firstTitle: Your first automation, step by step
guide.firstBody: The quickest way in is one of the ready-made ones on the first screen.
guide.firstPick: On the Automations screen, pick one from the gallery. Read the sentence underneath: that is exactly what it will do.
guide.firstUse: Press «Use this one». It becomes yours, and it is created switched off.
guide.firstFill: Fill in what it asked you to decide — an amount, a time, how long to wait. It always arrives with a sensible guess in place.
guide.firstAllow: Go to Permissions and allow what it needs. Until you do, it does nothing at all.
guide.firstTest: Press «Try it». It walks the automation against something that really happened in your business and shows you what it WOULD do — without sending, charging or writing anything down.
guide.firstEnable: Now turn it on with the switch at the top. From that moment it is watching, day and night.
guide.permissionsTitle: Permissions: why you have to say yes
guide.permissionsBody: An automation works while you are not looking, so it never borrows your own permissions. It can only do the exact things you allowed it, one by one — that is what stops it from ever doing more than you meant.
guide.permissionsWhere: You allow them inside the automation itself: open it and go to the Permissions tab. Everything it needs is listed there, with one button that allows the lot.
guide.permissionsNothing: An automation you never allowed anything is not broken and it is not slow: it simply does nothing, and it will not complain. If yours has never done a thing, look here first.
guide.historyBody: Open the automation and go to History. Every time it woke up there is a line with the day and the hour, and underneath it, in words, what it did.
guide.historyGuard: «The condition was not met, so it stopped here» is not a fault. That is the automation working: you told it to carry on only in certain cases, and this was not one of them.
guide.limitsBranches: There are no forks. An automation is one line of steps from top to bottom, and that is on purpose: if a condition is not met it stops there — it does not take a second route. Two different outcomes means two automations.
guide.limitsDates: It cannot count backwards from a date: «the day before the appointment» is not something it can work out yet. It can wait a while after something happened, which is not the same thing.
guide.limitsAssistant: And the assistant will not write the message step for you. Ask it for «tell them by message» and it leaves the closest thing it is allowed to propose — the job on your list — and says so in its own notes. Sending a message costs money every time, so that one is yours to add and yours to turn on.
